The agency today released a new global data set documenting changes in forest and land cover from 2000 through 2024. Built from satellite imagery at 30-meter resolution, the data set shows that the world lost approximately 4.1 million square kilometers of tree cover during that period, offset in part by regrowth and new plantations. Losses were concentrated in the tropics, where agricultural expansion remains the leading driver. The data are freely available online and are accompanied by documentation describing accuracy assessments, which indicate overall classification accuracy of 92 percent. Researchers said the product will support work on carbon accounting, biodiversity, and land management. The agency plans to update the data set annually and to add a layer identifying the cause of each loss event.
